title: ci: generate release graph and manifest validator for private-installer artifacts
author: Marcus Chen
description: Motivation: CI for private installer releases lacked a machine-readable release graph and a manifest-level validator that ties signed artifacts (images, helm charts, tf modules) back to the release manifest. This PR adds a release-graph generator and a manifest-validator stage to the private-installer CI pipeline to ensure provenance, enable safer upgrades/rollbacks, and block unsigned/unaligned manifests from publishing. Summary of changes: - new pipeline step 'build:release-graph' which produces a directed release graph (JSON) that maps artifacts -> helm chart values -> terraform module versions and includes cryptographic digests and SBOM references; graph is collated from build outputs and attestation metadata - new pipeline step 'validate:manifest' that consumes a release graph and enforces: cosign signature verification (keyless and KMS), SBOM presence, chart values checksum, and compatibility matrix checks for upgrades - small helper library under tools/release-graph that normalizes artifact metadata, computes canonical digests, and emits signatures-ready metadata for the signer job - Helm chart linting rules extended to emit a Helm manifest fingerprint (stable ordering) and surface mismatches between chart contents and release graph - Terraform module manifest extraction to include provider pins and a short policy check to prevent unsupported provider upgrades in the same release - CI orchestration changes: the validate step runs before artifact promotion and blocks publishing to the release bucket on failure - added an automated delta-rollback manifest generator which creates a minimal rollback plan from the release graph when a canary fails Why this is different: existing pipelines stamp artifacts and upload indexes, but we need a top-level release graph that can be consumed by Private control-plane for deterministic rollouts and by on-prem installers to reconcile manifests during upgrades. This PR focuses on making the release artifact a first-class, verifiable graph rather than loose indexes. Checklist: - [x] release-graph generator implemented - [x] manifest validator implemented and integrated into the CI workflow - [x] cosign verification (keyless and KMS) wired into validator - [x] Helm fingerprinting integrated - [x] Terraform module extraction implemented - [x] unit tests for tools/release-graph - [x] e2e run in staging that simulates signed artifact promotion - [x] added docs for ops on how to interpret the release graph Changes included (high level): tools/release-graph/* (new library and CLI), ci/pipeline/build-release-graph.yaml (new job), ci/pipeline/validate-manifest.yaml (new job), charts/private-installer/patches/manifest-fingerprint.yaml (helper), terraform/modules/release-metadata/README.md (docs), scripts/delta-rollback/gen-rollback.sh (new helper), tests/integration/release-graph-e2e (e2e harness). Testing and verification: - unit coverage for release-graph normalization functions - integration test that generates a release graph from staged artifacts, signs them with a test KMS key, then runs validator (CI job uses real cosign verification in staging) - staging rollout run that exercised the delta-rollback generator after a simulated canary failure - CI history shows two failed validator runs during early iteration (missing SBOMs) which were fixed by the chart/lint rule update Rollout plan: - merged to main and enabled in staging for one week; manual gating for production release (ops approval required) - enable automatic blocking on validator failures for subsequent releases; until then validator failures are opt-in via release-note flag Migration notes: - existing release index consumers must be updated to prefer release-graph.json; a small compatibility shim is provided under tools/release-graph/bin/compatify - operators must ensure cosign public key or KMS access is available in the Private control-plane to verify signatures Security considerations: - cosign key usage requires KMS scopes; the validator supports both keyless (OIDC) verification and KMS-backed verification; by default validator rejects unsigned artifacts - SBOM presence is mandatory for private installer releases; policy can be relaxed via a per-customer policy file if needed Documentation: - docs/private-installer/release-graph.md added explaining format and how to use the delta-rollback generator - ops playbook updated with steps to manually validate a release graph Known limitations & follow-ups: - release-graph currently serializes all digests in SHA256; we will add multi-algo support (ENG-6780 follow-up) - we do not yet have an automated remediation when validator fails (ENG-6723 will track a retry/auto-fix job) Related: ENG-6723 (release graph spec), ENG-6780 (multi-algo hashing), SUP-3048 (support ticket where customer asked for deterministic rollback plans).

review_comments: Priya Nair: Please add a note about KMS key rotation impact on old releases; we shouldn't make old releases unverifiable.
Marcus Chen: Added rotation doc and compatibility shim for cached public keys. See tools/release-graph/compat.md
Sofia Alvarez: Validator should surface which rule failed in CI summary. Added structured failure reasons to job output.

release_notes: Add release graph generation and manifest-level validation to private-installer CI. This enforces signed artifacts, SBOM presence, and compatibility checks before promoting releases. Also introduces a delta-rollback manifest generator for safer rollbacks.
footnotes: This PR intentionally keeps the release-graph format backward compatible via a small compat shim. Consumers are encouraged to migrate to release-graph.json.
Follow-ups tracked in ENG-6723 and ENG-6780.
